description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 from the coordinator's dig, a research prototype and a
cold review (BLOCK, with the precise prerequisite below). Base d2a5f3510.

THE MOVER: main/0 `return any` (FIFO) vs `list(int)` (LIFO). Mechanism
(return-ladder probe): under FIFO main first receives return evidence `any`
from the callsite target Kernel.dbg/1[([])], whose settled return IS `any`;
later `[] | [int]` arrives from dbg/1[([] | [int])]; ActivationMap::
define_return JOINS within an epoch and only a REBASE narrows, so main stays
`any`. LIFO never sees the intermediate target. (That join-only ladder is
fz-kdt.65 and stays.)

THE DEFECT: `@spec dbg(t) :: t when t: any; fn dbg(x), do: fz_dbg_value(x)`
should return its argument type; dbg([]) returns `any` while dbg([int]),
dbg(:a), dbg({}), dbg(%{}) return their own. Cause: types/arrow_match.rs
instantiate_match calls drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings (fz-f98.16),
which removes every variable binding a position collected through an exact
`[]` witness ("[] is a member of every list type, so a binding it pins is
noise"). MEASURED FACT: collect_instantiation_subst([a], []) binds NOTHING
(the element of [] is none; none-bindings are not collected), so the drop's
ONLY effect is to discard a variable bound to the WHOLE empty-list argument
-- exactly the case where the binding is a fact. Unit test
empty_list_binding_is_ambiguous ("Behavior 5") pins the defect.

THE RULE (research prototype, .kdt120/proto120.diff, survived 14 theorem
attacks): passing A to pattern P asserts A ⊆ σ(P); every variable in a
POSITIVE spot of P gets a LOWER bound, every variable under an arrow's
parameters an UPPER bound; merge_subst_union joins the lower bounds, so σ[v]
is the LEAST type satisfying the positive constraints observed so far -- and
that least solution is the answer IFF every positive occurrence contributed
its bound. A positive occurrence whose aligned ARGUMENT (never the witness:
overlapping_witnesses returns pattern-derived witnesses) is not ground
contributes nothing → v is OPEN → it may not instantiate the RESULT (a
published fact) but does instantiate the parameter surface. Carried through
the match walk as OpenVars { vars, positive }, flipped around
collect_arrow_match's argument descent; open_node_vars marks only the node's
own top-level vars; close_bounds seeded with the full substitution so an open
variable cannot fall back to its declared bound. Corollaries: [] at [a]
contributes the bottom bound (fz-f98.16 survives by construction); at a bare
a it IS the argument → dbg([]) : []; reduce(t(a), b, (a,b)->b) :: b with a
var-typed reducer leaves b open (the seed is a lower bound, not a fact);
filter(t(a), (a)->any) :: [a] at an unanalyzed lambda stays Known [int].
Two simpler rules were measured WRONG on the corpus and must not be
rebuilt: deleting the drop alone (7 wrong-answer movers -- the seed pins the
fold's accumulator, and reduce_finish({:done,a}|..)::a at the first ascent
rung {:done, []} is a genuine fact about a STALE rung) and "any var mentioned
by a position whose witness has vars is open" (38 movers: closure-literal
witnesses always carry var-typed arrows).

MEASURED under the prototype: dead_closure_capture_empty_list byte-identical
FIFO vs LIFO (main/0 return any → list(int)); 00277's [] component GONE on
both schedules (empty_list() mentions 480/479 → 76/76; the LIFO-only
dbg/1[empty_list()] pair and FIFO-only Range.reduce/5 {:cont, empty_list()}
rung both vanish; what remains is a joined-element key set, fz-kdt.124/the
blind-activation ticket); corpus `return any` 465 → 456, executables 5297 →
5276, no rise on any green fixture; f(a,a)::a at (int, []) was a FALSE
Invalid at HEAD, fixed; fz_f98_map_reduce (known-red) turns GREEN on three
doors; enum_tier0 prints the oracle exactly (still red on a library warning,
own ticket fz-kdt.185). BUT: enum_map_family turns RED with a phantom spec/violation
on `+/2` -- because at HEAD the @spec results were silently RE-CORRELATING
the joined return of List.reduce_step/3, an activation keyed entirely on free
type variables; honest Underconstrained results remove that accidental repair
and Enum.to_list/1[non_empty_list(binary)] publishes `return list(int |
binary)`, a false fact. No gate can mask it (the phantom and 00188's true
violation are structurally identical; disarming enforcement breaks 7
diagnostic fixtures and leaves the false fact). Q5's widening pin is the same
activation climbing 2 → 6 rungs, not headroom.

BLOCKED BY fz-kdt.183 (kill the blind activation / per-publisher return
correlation) and fz-kdt.184 (polarity-aware collection: merge_subst_union reads an
arrow parameter as a lower bound; A4 unsound, A5 false Invalid, pre-existing,
and the prototype's module doc claims the fix while the code lacks it).

LANDING SHAPE, once unblocked, one commit: the rule as prototyped; DELETE
drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings, collect_ambiguous_empty_list_vars,
is_exact_empty_list, "Behavior 5" and every "[] is ambiguous" sentence
(arrow_match.rs :55 vs :894 vocabulary split; .agent/docs/addressed-arrow.md
174-198 behavior 5 + both justification paragraphs + "cleans that position";
externs.md, specs.md, semantic-fixpoint.md, spec_shared_var_self_composition
header); a test for A9 (dbg(t)::t when t: any at a var-carrying argument goes
Known any → Underconstrained -- sound, must be stated); the widening pin
RE-DERIVED not re-pinned; fz_f98_map_reduce's three defer lines retired
(passes three doors); gates: dead_closure byte-identical FIFO/LIFO,
enum_tier0 NOT a new schedule mover, 0 behaviour movers, enum_map_family
green on three matrix doors. Known { result: [] | [int] } is acceptable
(fz-kdt.182 is not a prerequisite: [] | [T] activation keys 1 → 0).
title: A @spec variable is a lower bound and a fact only when every positive occurrence contributed: the empty-list ambiguity drop goes, dbg([]) is [], and dead_closure_capture_empty_list converges
